summary: This program counts down from 5 to 1, pausing one second between each number, then announces blastoff. It shows how a for loop can run backward using a third argument to range.

lines.text: The time module is part of Python's standard library, and it gives us the sleep function used below to make the countdown feel like a real countdown.

The third argument, -1, is the step: instead of adding 1 each pass, the loop subtracts 1. Since the loop stops before reaching the second number, the stop value must be 0 for the countdown to include 1.
Pausing the program for one second on each pass is what stretches the five numbers over five seconds rather than printing them all instantly.
This line sits outside the loop, with no indentation, so it runs once after the countdown finishes rather than after every number.
